- **Chris Olave** — Still dealing with blood-clot recovery, but the article is buying the dip and targeting him in the middle of the third round if ADP softens. Tom Brolley [2]

- **Parker Washington** — He looks like the Jaguars’ 2026 usage winner, with a larger route share likely and clear buy-low fantasy appeal after an efficient late-season stretch. Akash Bhatia [3]
- **Colston Loveland** — The article treats him like an elite rookie TE who can play as a real receiver, not just an in-line option, giving him breakout fantasy upside. Akash Bhatia [3]
- **Rome Odunze** — His breakout flashed before a possible lingering stress fracture, so the talent is still there but the health note adds uncertainty to his 2026 ceiling. Akash Bhatia [3]

DEN.summary:
- **Bo Nix (QB)** — Sean Payton said Nix did walkthrough work today and is expected to take part in next week’s mandatory minicamp; Payton added there are no concerns about his mobility once he’s back. That keeps Denver’s offense on track and signals Nix should be ready to resume full control before training camp. [1, 8]

- **Jaylen Waddle (WR)** — Waddle is already making noise at OTAs, with reports describing him as consistently explosive and stressing the defense even before Bo Nix returned to full work. That’s the kind of usage signal fantasy managers want from a high-end receiver: big-play ability, likely featured role, and an offense trying to build around him. [5]

- **Davis Webb (OC/play caller)** — Webb, now Denver’s play caller, said he wants to bring a different attitude while still operating within Sean Payton’s offensive philosophy. That matters because any shift in how aggressively the Broncos feature their weapons could change target distribution and overall pass-game ceiling. [3]

- **Talanoa Hufanga (S)** — Hufanga said he’s back on the JUGS machine after wrist surgery may have affected his hands last season, when dropped interceptions piled up. For IDP and splash-play formats, the takeaway is that his takeaway upside could improve if the ball skills rebound. [2]

- **Que Robinson (EDGE)** — Vance Joseph said Robinson looked like a future starter, and Sean Payton noted he handled a lot of special teams work last season and is progressing in year two. It’s not a direct fantasy bump, but it does point to a growing defensive role and more game-day snaps. [4]
